summary: Enable contextual channel-tagging and daily thread-digest Slack bot with Confluence metadata sync
description:
Request: Provision a scoped Slack automation that can (1) read Confluence page metadata for project/channel mappings and automatically apply channel topic/tags, and (2) produce a daily digest of active threads in specified channels and post a summarized thread into a pinned channel.

Impact: Reduce manual tagging of channels, improve discoverability for cross-pod collaboration, and provide lightweight async summaries to reduce meeting load. This will be used by runbook/ops channels and a few product pods on an opt-in basis.

Requirements:
- A bot service account with least-privilege scopes (read channel metadata, set channel topic/purpose, read pinned messages, post messages).
- Confluence-to-Slack mapping configuration: a Confluence page or page-space that contains a table of channel -> metadata (tags, retention policy, owner).
- Daily job (09:00 UTC) that aggregates top 10 active threads per channel, runs an extractive summary, and posts a single digest message with links.
- Ephemeral channel lifecycle hooks: when retention TTL set in Confluence mapping expires, send an automatic ownership ping and a 7-day deletion warning to the channel.
- Audit log entries written to an internal Confluence/ops page and a Jira ticket for each deletion action.

Acceptance criteria:
- Slack bot created and visible in org apps with documented scopes.
- Admin page (Confluence) editable by ops to control mappings and TTLs.
- Daily digest posts in #ops-digests and can be disabled per-channel via mapping.
- RBAC: only approved admins can modify mappings; bot cannot escalate permissions.

Notes: This is an internal-support automation; sensitive operations (channel deletion) must be gated and logged. We prefer a phased rollout: start with 5 pilot channels (ops-runbooks, infra-alerts, platform-rt) before broad enablement.
